contract: act(instruction: str, observation: str, valid_actions: list[str], history: list[tuple[str, str, float]], llm) -> str: the next action. `instruction` is the episode's fixed task text, `observation` the environment's latest text, `valid_actions` the actions the environment lists for this state (empty when it lists none), `history` the (action, observation, reward) triples of the current episode and `llm(prompt_or_messages, system=None, max_tokens=None, temperature=None, json_mode=False) -> str` a budgeted, cached OpenRouter chat client. act must return a str (anything else invalidates the evaluation); a crash or timeout ends the episode with the environment's score at that point; exhausting the model budget invalidates the evaluation. The agent runs in a sandboxed child process (one per episode; module state persists within an episode only) that sees nothing but these arguments. Environment: M3ToolEval (CodeAct) in text-as-action mode: `instruction` is CodeAct's task prompt with the tool list, each reply is one assistant turn ('Action: tool, arg, ... End Action' or 'Answer: ...'), `observation` the tool result or feedback; a fixed sample of 4 tasks per domain (20 episodes), at most 10 turns. Episode score: 1 when solved, else 0. Score: success rate over the 20 episodes; higher is better
notes: Environment: CodeAct's own M3ToolEval task package (xingyaoww/code-act at commit d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8, scripts/eval/m3tooleval, MIT), fetched by scripts/prepare_agent_bench.py and imported with one replacement: CodeAct's `calculator` tool is eval(expression), which would execute the agent's text as Python in the environment server next to the expected outputs; it is replaced by an arithmetic evaluator (numbers, + - * / // % **, parentheses, abs, round, int, float; integers up to 4096 bits), and every other expression gets CodeAct's 'Failed to evaluate expression' reply. Its IPython-based REPL, needed only for the code-as-action mode, and its tqdm progress bar are stubbed out. Turns follow CodeAct's run_task: post-processing to the first Action/Answer block, CodeAct's parser, tool execution, the 'incorrect, try again' message after a wrong answer, success on a correct answer or (for single-tool tasks) a tool result equal to the expected output, 10-turn limit. AgentSquare's own runner also accepts a correct answer at any turn within 10 turns.
Action mode: text-as-action (CodeAct's default, the mode AgentSquare runs); the JSON and code modes are not offered.
Sample: AgentSquare evaluates all 82 tasks of the five domains; here a fixed sample of 4 tasks per domain (20) in SHA-256 order (seed 0).

Candidate: AgentSquare searches over agent module code (planning, reasoning, tool use, memory with a uniform interface) with module evolution, recombination and a performance predictor; those belong to the search method. Here the candidate is the agent program itself, act(...) called once per step; it may implement any modules internally. The AgentSquare repository has no licence, so its code is only read to recover the protocol; the environments come from the benchmarks' own releases.

Model: AgentSquare runs GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 and GPT-4o; the default client model here is google/gemini-2.5-flash at temperature 0 (ARTASK_LLM_MODEL overrides it), so absolute scores are not comparable with the paper. Not verified: the paper's numbers were not reproduced.

Isolation: the candidate runs in a resource-limited child process (software_sandbox) that cannot read files outside the Python installation; model calls and steps are forwarded to the evaluator, and the environment (including any gold plan or answer) runs in a separate server process, so the candidate cannot see labels or solutions.

Model-driven agent evaluation: the score is an estimate on a fixed, seeded list of episodes and depends on the model (ARTASK_LLM_MODEL, default google/gemini-2.5-flash at temperature 0) and on the per-evaluation budget (task parameter budget_usd, overridden by ARTASK_LLM_BUDGET_USD); exhausting the budget makes the evaluation invalid. ARTASK_AGENT_EPISODES truncates the episode list for quick checks. The candidate runs in a resource-limited child process (one per episode) that receives only the instruction, observations, listed valid actions, its own history and a model client; the environment runs in a separate server process. Responses are cached under llm-cache of the task cache. `valid` is null because a sampled model score cannot certify a candidate.
protocol_description: Locally implemented or adapted evaluator for the cited task or benchmark. Data sources, generated instances, evaluation budgets and protocol differences are specified in the candidate contract, requirements and notes; scores are not automatically comparable with published results.
name: M3ToolEval
description: Write a Python act(instruction, observation, valid_actions, history, llm) agent that solves M3ToolEval tasks by calling tools or answering in CodeAct's text-as-action format, using a budgeted OpenRouter model client; scored by the success rate over 20 fixed tasks (4 per domain), at most 10 turns each (higher is better).

sources.locator: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1 (tasks and metrics)
tasks, tools, prompt, parser and answer check (used unchanged)

limitations: CodeAct's answer check converts the expected output with int() before comparing, so for a non-integer expected number it also accepts the integer part (expected 161.25: '161' is accepted). This affects 14 of the 82 tasks and 4 of the 20 sampled ones; the check is kept because it is the benchmark's own.

The 20 episodes are a fixed list of public benchmark items that every evaluation replays, and act may return actions without calling the model. A program that replays memorised answers or actions for these episodes is scored like an agent, so the score says nothing about other episodes of the benchmark.
